correctness.rationale: Definitions include empty word, binary alphabet, Dyck balance, exact subsequence index and all integer boundaries. Greedy arch equivalence is explicitly justified. Multiplication of the actual three-state zero/one matrices under the unique Dyck first-return grammar yields four formal power-series equations; the constant-term unit forces c=0, after which exact elimination proves (1-t)(H-1)=tu(1-tu)H^2. Catalan substitution and coefficient extraction give all n,k, and the unique maximal-degree term j=k gives C_k/(k-1)!. The packaged verification independently checks all Dyck words through semilength 8 by direct pattern subsequence tests, recurrence coefficients through 27, and Catalan finite differences through index 17. Finite tests corroborate but do not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: Dyck excursions are the standard nonregular Catalan language and binary subsequence universality is a natural global containment invariant. The new closed bivariate algebraic law solves every length/index count, exhibits an exact Catalan polynomial hierarchy at fixed index, and recovers Catalan row sums. These consequences go beyond textbook Catalan enumeration or a small finite slice and can support exact random-Dyck containment probabilities.
